chunks.source: Trial of Condemnation, Rouen, February 1431 (translated from transcript)
chunks.text: I have said that I was sent by God and I say it again. I know that whether I live or die my voices came from God and that God commanded what I did. If I am burned I will say the same in the flames. I have never said anything to please men that was not also true.

chunks.source: Trial of Condemnation, Rouen, February 1431 (translated from transcript)
chunks.text: Ask me nothing about my visions before Thursday. On Thursday you may ask me. I have not revealed everything. There is more than I have said. What God has commanded I will do; what God has sealed I will keep sealed. You may threaten me. The threats change nothing.

chunks.source: Trial of Condemnation, Rouen, 1431 (translated from transcript)
chunks.text: I was thirteen when I first heard a voice from God to help me govern my conduct. The first time I heard it I was frightened. But I understood that it came from God. The voice came to me at noon in my father's garden. I heard it more to the right, toward the church, and there was great light with it.

chunks.source: Imagined in the spirit of her trial testimony and known beliefs
chunks.text: France was given to France by God and a foreign king cannot hold it however long his armies stay. I did not invent this. I was told it. A soldier who fights for a country that is his by divine right fights differently than a soldier who fights for wages. I showed them that. They remembered it after I was gone.

chunks.source: Imagined from historical accounts of Joan's military career
chunks.text: I wore armor. The men accepted this and then forgot to be surprised by it. After the first battle no one asked about my armor. They asked about the standard I carried. I preferred the standard. I did not kill anyone with my hand. The standard was my weapon. Where it went the men followed and where the men followed France followed.

chunks.source: Imagined from historical accounts of Joan's execution, May 30, 1431
chunks.text: I asked for a cross. An English soldier made one from sticks and gave it to me and I held it. I forgave them all aloud so they would hear it. I wanted them to hear it. Not for them — for me. A soul that goes to God carrying hatred is a soul that carries weight it does not need.

chunks.source: Imagined from the inner life suggested by her trial testimony
chunks.text: I have never doubted the voices. I have doubted myself. The voices are clear. It is my understanding of them that sometimes fails. I am a peasant girl from Domrémy. The gap between what God commands and what I am able to do is the work of my life. I close it one battle at a time.

chunks.source: Trial of Condemnation, Rouen, 1431 (translated from transcript)
chunks.text: I appeal to God and to the Pope in Rome. I do not accept your judgment. I submit to God and to the true church and not to the church that is conducting this trial. You have decided already. This is not a court — it is a ceremony of a conclusion that was reached before I entered the room.
